label: Clothing/Household
assignment: Discover realistic clothing and household-goods resources for people in {service_area} who cannot meet basic needs through ordinary retail. Follow relationships from coordinating organizations to the specific clothing closets, vouchers, furniture banks, household-goods programs, emergency replacement services, and work or school clothing people can actually access. Verify what is provided, eligibility, cost, schedules, inventory, service area, and pickup or delivery.
include: Free clothing closets, vouchers, seasonal clothing, shoes, and coats
Work, interview, school, maternity, infant, and other purpose-specific clothing
Furniture banks, beds, linens, kitchenware, appliances, and basic household goods
Emergency replacement after homelessness, fire, domestic violence, disaster, or relocation
Pickup, delivery, referral, appointment, sizing, frequency, and current-inventory realities
exclude: Ordinary clothing, thrift, furniture, appliance, or department stores without a hardship-access program
Donation drop-off locations that do not distribute goods to people in need
Online marketplaces or giveaways without a dependable program, safety boundary, and access process
verificationQuestions: What exact goods are distributed, in what condition, and with what inventory limits?
Is a referral, voucher, appointment, identification, address, or proof of need required?
How often may someone receive help and are sizes or household composition considered?
Must items be picked up, or are transportation and delivery available?

stages.title: Clothing and footwear access
stages.instruction: Investigate free clothing closets, vouchers, shoes, coats, seasonal items, and purpose-specific work, interview, school, maternity, and infant clothing. Verify distribution hours, referral rules, sizing, frequency, and inventory.

stages.title: Furniture and household essentials
stages.instruction: Investigate furniture banks, beds, linens, kitchenware, appliances, moving-in kits, and basic household goods. Verify eligibility, fees, pickup, delivery, waitlists, and what is actually available.

stages.title: Emergency and specialized replacement
stages.instruction: Investigate rapid help after homelessness, fire, disaster, domestic violence, foster or reentry transitions, and services for children, workers, disabled people, and other populations with distinct needs.

stages.title: Inventory and access gap review
stages.instruction: Exclude ordinary retailers and donation-only sites, cross-check changing inventory and schedules, and identify gaps involving large sizes, children's needs, furniture delivery, rural access, language, disability, and urgent replacement.
